Finally, in the scale--invariant case $β=0$, a concentration--compactness analysis proves that the inequality's sharp constant is achieved by an optimal function, with minimizing sequences remaining precompact up to the natural three-parameter group of symmetries.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes weighted Gagliardo--Nirenberg interpolation inequalities for Grushin-type operators on R^n x R^m, determining exact and optimal parameter conditions, and proves sharp-constant attainability in the scale-invariant case.
AI.motivation: The authors aim to understand how weighted norms can be controlled by balancing fractional and weighted derivatives for Grushin-type operators, extending classical Gagliardo--Nirenberg interpolation to this degenerate, multi-parameter setting.
AI.method: The analysis combines two-parameter scaling, spatial translations, Littlewood--Paley decompositions, Khintchine-type random sums for multi-parameter extensions, geometric covering arguments, a generalized three-norm Strauss lemma, and concentration--compactness techniques.
AI.result: Exact parameter conditions are derived, with scaling exponents shown necessary and optimal. Radial symmetry enlarges the allowable weight range and restores compact embeddings into L^p (2<p<B), with explicit pointwise weighted decay. For beta=0, the sharp constant is attained, and minimizing sequences are precompact up to the three-parameter symmetry group. Q>=2 is strictly required for multi-parameter weighted extensions.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a complete characterization of weighted Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequalities for Grushin-type operators, including optimality, compactness under radial symmetry, and existence of extremals in the scale-invariant regime.

title: Strichartz estimates for Klein-Gordon equations on asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds with applications
comment: 28 pages, 1 figures. All comments are welcome
summary: In this paper, we establish global-in-time Strichartz estimates for Klein-Gordon equations on non-trapping asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds. Our result is a positive-mass counterpart of the global Strichartz estimates of Sire, Sogge, Wang, and Zhang for shifted wave equations, and recovers the same range of admissible pairs. The main new feature is the low-frequency analysis, where the positive mass changes the spectral phase and leads to a different dispersive mechanism. Combining the resulting low-frequency estimates with microlocalized high-frequency estimates yields the full global Strichartz estimates. As applications, we obtain small-data global existence and scattering for power-type and certain derivative semilinear equations, as well as small-data global existence for a class of smooth semilinear equations without imposing a null condition.

AI.tldr: This paper proves global-in-time Strichartz estimates for Klein-Gordon equations on non-trapping asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds, handling low-frequency analysis where positive mass alters the dispersive mechanism, and applies the results to semilinear equations.
AI.motivation: The work extends the global Strichartz estimates of Sire, Sogge, Wang, and Zhang for shifted wave equations to the positive-mass Klein-Gordon case on non-trapping asymptotically hyperbolic manifolds.
AI.method: Low-frequency analysis addressing the spectral phase change from positive mass, combined with microlocalized high-frequency estimates to obtain full global Strichartz estimates.
AI.result: Global Strichartz estimates are established, recovering the same range of admissible pairs as in the shifted wave equation case.
AI.conclusion: Applications include small-data global existence and scattering for power-type and certain derivative semilinear equations, plus small-data global existence for a class of smooth semilinear equations without a null condition.

title: Unique mild solution for the ES-BGK model with the correct Prandtl number
summary: We prove the existence and uniqueness of mild solutions to the ellipsoidal BGK (ES-BGK) model with the correct Prandtl number, under suitable weighted bounds and a free-transport non-vacuum condition. At the correct Prandtl number, the temperature tensor is no longer uniformly comparable to the scalar temperature, so classical scalar moment estimates do not directly yield the required Gaussian bounds. We derive anisotropic velocity moment estimates by splitting velocity space along the longest principal direction of the stress tensor and using the geometry of transverse elliptical slices. These estimates yield a linear weighted $L^{\infty}$ bound for the ellipsoidal Gaussian. Together with uniform ellipticity and weighted $L^1$-Lipschitz continuity under the stated assumptions, this bound allows us to construct unique mild solutions.

AI.tldr: The paper proves existence and uniqueness of mild solutions to the ellipsoidal BGK (ES-BGK) model with the correct Prandtl number, using anisotropic velocity moment estimates and a linear weighted L-infinity bound for the ellipsoidal Gaussian.
AI.motivation: At the correct Prandtl number, the temperature tensor is no longer uniformly comparable to the scalar temperature, so classical scalar moment estimates fail to yield the needed Gaussian bounds, requiring a new approach for the ES-BGK model.
AI.method: The authors assume suitable weighted bounds and a free-transport non-vacuum condition. They derive anisotropic velocity moment estimates by splitting velocity space along the longest principal direction of the stress tensor and exploiting the geometry of transverse elliptical slices, yielding a linear weighted L-infinity bound, used together with uniform ellipticity and weighted L1-Lipschitz continuity.
AI.result: The anisotropic estimates produce a linear weighted L-infinity bound for the ellipsoidal Gaussian, enabling construction of mild solutions.
AI.conclusion: Existence and uniqueness of mild solutions to the ES-BGK model with the correct Prandtl number is established under the stated assumptions.

title: Coarse ellipticity and De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory in the optimal range
summary: We extend the theory of De Giorgi-Nash-Moser to elliptic equations with symmetric coefficients $\mathbf{a}(x)$ which are possibly degenerate and unbounded but satisfy a coarse ellipticity condition. We prove local upper bounds for weak subsolutions, a weak Harnack inequality for nonnegative supersolutions, and a Harnack inequality for nonnegative solutions. The coarse ellipticity hypothesis requires spatial moments of coarse-grained matrices, suitably discounted and summed across scales, to be finite. In particular, it holds if, for some $α,β\geq0$ and $1<p,q<\infty$, $$\mathbf{a}\in W^{-α,p}\cap L^1, \quad \mathbf{a}^{-1}\in W^{-β,q}\cap L^1 \quad\text{and}\quad \frac{α+β}{2}+\frac{d-1}{2}\Big(\frac1p+\frac1q\Big)<1.$$ We show that the coefficient range is sharp, including its boundary, in every dimension $d\geq3$, for $α=β=0$ and for the corresponding Besov-type quasi-norms of negative order when $α,β>0$. For $α=β=0$, it corresponds to the results of Bella and Schäffner [8].

AI.tldr: The paper extends De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory to elliptic equations with symmetric, possibly degenerate and unbounded coefficients satisfying a coarse ellipticity condition, proving local upper bounds, a weak Harnack inequality, and a Harnack inequality, with sharp coefficient range.
AI.motivation: Classical De Giorgi-Nash-Moser theory assumes bounded, uniformly elliptic coefficients. This work aims to relax these assumptions to allow degenerate and unbounded symmetric coefficients, capturing a broader class of equations via a coarse ellipticity condition.
AI.method: The authors impose a coarse ellipticity hypothesis requiring spatial moments of coarse-grained matrices, discounted and summed across scales, to be finite. This condition is characterized via negative-order Sobolev/Besov-type norms, e.g., a in W^{-α,p} ∩ L^1 and a^{-1} in W^{-β,q} ∩ L^1 under a specific inequality on α, β, p, q, d.
AI.result: They prove local upper bounds for weak subsolutions, a weak Harnack inequality for nonnegative supersolutions, and a Harnack inequality for nonnegative solutions. The coefficient range is shown to be sharp, including its boundary, in every dimension d ≥ 3, for α = β = 0 and for the corresponding Besov-type quasi-norms when α, β > 0.
AI.conclusion: The theory generalizes De Giorgi-Nash-Moser to degenerate and unbounded coefficients. The sharpness results recover and extend prior work (Bella and Schäffner for α = β = 0), confirming the optimality of the ellipticity condition.

title: Uniqueness of pressureless flow
summary: We consider the pressureless Euler equations in one spatial dimension. These equations model the dynamics of particles on a line that interact only through perfectly inelastic collisions. The flow was first shown to be unique for given initial conditions by Huang and Wang, assuming the entropy and the strong initial continuity of energy conditions hold. In this paper, we prove an analogous uniqueness theorem using a Lagrangian interpretation. The key ingredients are showing that each solution satisfying the entropy condition and an initial kinetic energy bound has this particular type of Lagrangian interpretation and a monotonicity inequality involving conditional expectation.

AI.tldr: This paper proves a uniqueness theorem for the pressureless Euler equations in 1D using a Lagrangian interpretation, assuming entropy and an initial kinetic energy bound.
AI.motivation: Huang and Wang first proved uniqueness of the flow for given initial conditions under entropy and strong initial continuity of energy conditions. This paper aims to provide an analogous uniqueness result via a Lagrangian perspective.
AI.method: The proof shows that each solution satisfying the entropy condition and an initial kinetic energy bound admits a particular Lagrangian interpretation, combined with a monotonicity inequality involving conditional expectation.
AI.result: A uniqueness theorem analogous to Huang and Wang's is established using the Lagrangian interpretation framework.
AI.conclusion: Uniqueness of solutions to the 1D pressureless Euler equations can be recovered through a Lagrangian interpretation with a conditional-expectation monotonicity inequality.

title: Ground States of a Transversely Confined Polaron: Uniqueness and an Explicit Limiting Profile
summary: We study minimizers of the Pekar functional with a transverse harmonic potential, which models a polaron harmonically trapped in the transverse plane but free along the longitudinal direction. For any confinement strength $Ω>0$, minimizers exist and, up to a translation along the $x_3$-direction, are radially decreasing in $(x_1,x_2)$ and symmetric decreasing in $x_3$. For small $Ω>0$ we prove uniqueness up to these symmetries. For sufficiently large $Ω>0$ we derive a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy and show that, after a suitable rescaling, the minimizers converge in $H^1(\mathbb{R}^3)\cap L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^3)$ to the product of the normalized ground state of a two-dimensional linear harmonic oscillator and that of an effective one-dimensional nonlinear local problem, displaying asymptotic variable separation. This gives, for the transversely confined Pekar model, a rigorous ground-state counterpart of the three-dimensional-to-one-dimensional dimension-reduction phenomenon numerically observed for Coulomb-type Schrödinger equations with anisotropic confining potentials in [W. Z. Bao, H. Y. Jian, N. J. Mauser and Y. Zhang, SIAM J. Appl. Math., 2013]. Moreover, uniqueness up to the same symmetries is also established for all sufficiently large $Ω>0$.

AI.tldr: Analysis of minimizers of the Pekar functional with transverse harmonic confinement, establishing existence, symmetries, uniqueness, and asymptotic dimension reduction for large confinement.
AI.motivation: The Pekar functional models a polaron; the transversely trapped, longitudinally free setting arises in physics. The paper aims to rigorously justify the dimension-reduction phenomenon (3D to 1D) previously observed numerically for Coulomb-type Schrödinger equations with anisotropic confining potentials.
AI.method: Variational analysis of minimizers of the Pekar functional with a transverse harmonic potential. Uses concentration/compactness arguments for existence, rearrangement/moving-plane techniques for symmetry, and asymptotic analysis for small and large confinement strength Ω.
AI.result: For any Ω>0 minimizers exist and are radially decreasing in (x1,x2) and symmetric decreasing in x3 (up to translation). For small Ω, uniqueness up to these symmetries. For large Ω, a three-term asymptotic expansion of the ground state energy, and convergence (after rescaling) in H^1∩L^∞ to a product of a 2D harmonic oscillator ground state and an effective 1D nonlinear problem, showing asymptotic variable separation. Uniqueness holds for all sufficiently large Ω.
AI.conclusion: The work provides a rigorous ground-state counterpart of the numerically observed 3D-to-1D dimension reduction for the transversely confined Pekar model, with full symmetry, uniqueness, and asymptotic results.

title: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation in an exterior domain
summary: We study the exact controllability of the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the exterior $Ω=\mathbb{R}^n\setminusΘ$ of a non-trapping obstacle $Θ$, with internal controls supported outside a large ball, and the corresponding boundary control problem on $Ω_0=B_{R_0}\setminusΘ$ with Dirichlet controls acting only on the outer sphere $\partial B_{R_0}$. Using the local smoothing effect of Burq, Gérard and Tzvetkov [9], we prove observability inequalities for the linear Schrödinger equation in the whole scale of Sobolev spaces $H^σ_D(Ω)$, $σ\in[-2,2]$, associated with the Dirichlet Laplacian; they require only the non-trapping assumption (no star-shapedness of $Θ$), and their proofs use no normal boundary traces. Combined with Strichartz-type estimates and a perturbation argument, this yields local exact controllability in $H^1_0(Ω)$ and in $H^2(Ω)\cap H^1_0(Ω)$, in dimensions two and three, around the zero solution and, for internal controls and under a unique continuation assumption, around nontrivial trajectories. The same method applies to the quintic equation, which is energy-critical in dimension three. Several open problems are discussed.

AI.tldr: The paper proves local exact controllability of the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation in the exterior of a non-trapping obstacle (and on a related bounded domain via outer-boundary Dirichlet controls), using observability inequalities for the linear Schrödinger equation across Sobolev spaces H^σ_D, σ∈[-2,2].
AI.motivation: Controllability of nonlinear dispersive equations on domains with obstacles is largely open, especially beyond star-shaped geometries. The authors aim to remove geometric restrictions (like star-shapedness) and handle controls acting only away from the obstacle or on the outer boundary.
AI.method: They use the local smoothing effect of Burq–Gérard–Tzvetkov to prove observability inequalities for the linear Schrödinger equation in the full scale H^σ_D(Ω), σ∈[-2,2], requiring only the non-trapping assumption and avoiding normal boundary traces. These are combined with Strichartz-type estimates and a perturbation argument.
AI.result: They obtain local exact controllability in H^1_0(Ω) and H^2(Ω)∩H^1_0(Ω) in dimensions two and three, around the zero solution and, for internal controls under a unique continuation assumption, around nontrivial trajectories. The method also applies to the quintic equation, energy-critical in dimension three.
AI.conclusion: The approach yields new controllability results for NLS in non-trapping exterior domains without star-shapedness, and extends to the quintic (energy-critical) case; several open problems are discussed.

title: Instantaneous gap loss of Sobolev regularity for the surface quasi-geostrophic equation
summary:
We prove instantaneous loss of Sobolev regularity across a fixed gap for the inviscid surface quasi-geostrophic equation on $\mathbb R^2$. More precisely, for every $1<s<2$, $T>0$ and $\varepsilon>0$, we construct initial data $θ_0\in H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ with $\|θ_0\|_{H^s}\leq\varepsilon$ that generate a solution $θ$ on $[0,T]$ such that
  \[
  θ\in L^\infty([0,T];H^{1+γ}(\mathbb R^2)),
  \quad
  θ(t)\notin H^σ(\mathbb R^2)
  \quad\text{for every }t\in(0,T],\ σ>σ_*(s),
  \]
  where $γ>0$ and $σ_*(s)$ satisfy
  \[
  1+γ<σ_*(s):=
  \frac{s(3-s)}{1+2s-s^2}<s.
  \]
  The solution is unique in a determined family of classical solutions with initial datum $θ_0$.

AI.tldr: The paper proves instantaneous loss of Sobolev regularity across a fixed gap for the inviscid surface quasi-geostrophic (SQG) equation on R^2, constructing arbitrarily small H^s initial data whose unique solutions immediately fail to be in H^σ for σ>σ_*(s), where 1+γ<σ_*(s)<s.
AI.motivation: Understanding regularity behavior of the inviscid SQG equation is a central problem in fluid dynamics and PDE theory. Sharp regularity thresholds, especially instantaneous (in-time) loss of smoothness, reveal strong non-linear instability. This work aims to establish such loss across a fixed gap below the initial Sobolev exponent s.
AI.method: A constructive approach: for each 1<s<2, T>0, ε>0, the authors build initial data θ_0 in H^s with small norm ≤ ε. They then analyze the resulting solution θ, showing it lies in L^∞([0,T];H^{1+γ}) but escapes H^σ for σ>σ_*(s) at every positive time. Uniqueness is established within a determined family of classical solutions.
AI.result: For every 1<s<2, T>0, ε>0, there exist initial data θ_0∈H^s with ‖θ_0‖_{H^s}≤ε generating solutions on [0,T] satisfying θ∈L^∞([0,T];H^{1+γ}) and θ(t)∉H^σ for all t∈(0,T], σ>σ_*(s), where σ_*(s)=s(3−s)/(1+2s−s^2).
AI.conclusion: The inviscid SQG equation exhibits instantaneous loss of Sobolev regularity across a gap, with solutions that are arbitrarily small in H^s yet immediately fail to belong to H^σ beyond the threshold σ_*(s). The uniqueness within a specific class reinforces the sharpness of the construction.

title: Hölder Gradient Estimates for $(s,p)$-Poisson Equations with measurable and Hölder Data
summary: We prove interior $C^{1,α}$ estimates for weak solutions of the fractional $p$-Poisson equation, with $p\geq2$. For right-hand sides in $L^q$, we obtain the estimate when $p<(1-d/q)/(1-s)$. For $γ$-Hölder continuous right-hand sides, the range is $p<(1+γ)/(1-s)$. Both ranges of parameters are optimal.

AI.tldr: This paper proves optimal interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimates for weak solutions of the fractional $p$-Poisson equation with $p\ge2$, with sharp parameter ranges for $L^q$ and Hölder right-hand sides.
AI.motivation: Regularity theory for fractional $p$-Laplace-type equations is less developed than for the classical local case, and sharp conditions on the right-hand side for $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity were not fully determined.
AI.method: Analytic PDE techniques: establish interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimates for weak solutions of the fractional $p$-Poisson equation, treating $L^q$ right-hand sides (valid for $p<(1-d/q)/(1-s)$) and $\gamma$-Hölder right-hand sides (valid for $p<(1+\gamma)/(1-s)$).
AI.result: Interior $C^{1,\alpha}$ estimates are obtained under the stated conditions, and both parameter ranges are shown to be optimal.
AI.conclusion: The work provides sharp interior regularity for the fractional $p$-Poisson equation, with optimal ranges depending on integrability or Hölder regularity of the right-hand side.

title: A Kinetic Concentration criterion for Large-data Boltzmann Dynamics
summary:
We establish a conditional theory of genuinely non-perturbative global dynamics for the cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials on the three-dimensional torus. We prove that any global mild solution satisfying \[ \sup_{t\ge0}\int_{\mathbb R^3}W(v)\sup_{x\in\mathbb T^3}F(t,x,v)\,dv<\infty, \] for a suitable stretched-exponential weight \(W\), enjoys uniform weighted \(L^\infty\) control, is unique in the dissipative mild class, and converges exponentially to the global Maxwellian. In particular, these conclusions hold for arbitrary-amplitude solutions admitting a uniform stretched-exponential velocity upper bound.
  The key mechanism is a *tail-to-coercivity principle*: uniform velocity-tail control generates positive lower bounds for the local density and nonlinear collision frequency, without imposing macroscopic coercivity a priori. A double-Duhamel positivity argument also generates a Gaussian lower bound at arbitrarily short positive times, allowing initial data with local vacuum.
  We establish a polynomially weighted counterpart under an additional spatially uniform lower velocity profile, obtaining analogous weighted \(L^\infty\) bounds, uniqueness, and exponential relaxation.
  Our results provide a low-regularity alternative to conditional theories requiring smoothness and pointwise macroscopic bounds. They reveal how a single velocity-tail condition controls large-data Boltzmann dynamics and suggest a route toward problems with physical boundary conditions.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a conditional theory for genuinely non-perturbative global dynamics of the cutoff Boltzmann equation with hard potentials on the 3D torus, showing that a uniform stretched-exponential velocity-tail bound yields weighted L∞ control, uniqueness, and exponential convergence to Maxwellian.
AI.motivation: Existing conditional theories for large-data Boltzmann dynamics typically require smoothness and pointwise macroscopic bounds. The authors seek a low-regularity alternative in which a single velocity-tail condition suffices to control large-data dynamics, without assuming macroscopic coercivity a priori.
AI.method: They prove conditional results for global mild solutions satisfying a sup-in-time integral velocity bound with a stretched-exponential weight W. The core mechanism is a 'tail-to-coercivity principle': uniform velocity-tail control yields positive lower bounds on local density and nonlinear collision frequency. A double-Duhamel positivity argument generates Gaussian lower bounds at short positive times, permitting locally vacuum initial data. A polynomially weighted analogue is derived under an extra spatially uniform lower velocity profile.
AI.result: Any global mild solution obeying the weighted tail bound enjoys uniform weighted L∞ control, uniqueness in the dissipative mild class, and exponential convergence to the global Maxwellian, including arbitrary-amplitude solutions with a uniform stretched-exponential velocity upper bound. The polynomially weighted counterpart yields analogous weighted L∞ bounds, uniqueness, and exponential relaxation.
AI.conclusion: A single velocity-tail condition can control large-data Boltzmann dynamics, giving a low-regularity alternative to conditional theories needing smoothness and pointwise macroscopic bounds, and suggesting a route toward problems with physical boundary conditions.

title: Invariant manifolds and transversality for a traveling-wave ODE in a controlled reaction-diffusion model
summary: We study the parameter dependence and transversality properties of trajectories of the controlled ODE $$ U_x = P, \qquad P_x = - f(U) - βP + \tilde α(x)U, $$ arising from traveling-wave solutions of a bistable reaction-diffusion equation with control. Optimal profiles minimizing the $L^1$-norm of the control $\tilde α$ are determined by the unstable and stable manifolds $Γ_u$, $Γ_s$, the critical curve $$ P^*(U) = \sqrt{Uf(U)}, $$ and the associated function $$ F(U) = \frac{dP^*}{dU} + \frac{f(U)}{P^*(U)}. $$ We establish generic transversality properties for these objects with respect to perturbations of the speed $β$ and the nonlinear source $f$, together with quantitative estimates on the first- and second-order dependence of the invariant manifolds on these parameters. We also analyze the loss of regularity at the critical speed $β^{**}$, where the unstable manifold approaches the strongly stable manifold of the equilibrium $(U^*,0)$. These results provide the ODE ingredients used in the analysis of the structure and regularity of optimal profiles in paper [S. Bianchini and C. Trifone. Traveling profiles and control cost for a PDE describing the evolution of invasive species. 2026. arXiv: 2606.23979 [math.OC]].

AI.tldr: The paper studies parameter dependence and transversality of trajectories of a controlled ODE from traveling-wave solutions of a bistable reaction-diffusion equation, deriving generic transversality and quantitative estimates for optimal control profiles.
AI.motivation: This work provides the ODE ingredients needed to analyze the structure and regularity of optimal profiles in a companion PDE paper on invasive species evolution.
AI.method: Analyzes the controlled ODE U_x = P, P_x = -f(U) - βP + α̃(x)U, using the stable/unstable manifolds Γ_u, Γ_s, the critical curve P*(U)=√(Uf(U)), and F(U)=dP*/dU + f(U)/P*(U); establishes generic transversality with respect to perturbations of β and f, with first- and second-order dependence estimates of invariant manifolds.
AI.result: Generic transversality properties are established, quantitative first- and second-order dependence of invariant manifolds on parameters is obtained, and loss of regularity at the critical speed β** (where the unstable manifold approaches the strongly stable manifold of (U*,0)) is analyzed.
AI.conclusion: The results supply the ODE framework used to study the structure and regularity of optimal profiles in Bianchini and Trifone (2026).

title: (In)finiteness of slopes for Monge-Ampère equations at flat boundary pieces
summary:
On any bounded convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with a $d$-dimensional flat boundary piece $F\subset\partialΩ$, we consider convex solutions with zero boundary values to the Monge-Ampère equations
  $$
  \det\mathsf{D}^2 u= \mathrm{dist}(\,\cdot\,,\mathrm{Aff}(F))^α,\quad\det\mathsf{D}^2 u=\mathrm{dist}(\,\cdot\,,\partialΩ)^α,\quad \det\mathsf{D}^2 u=(-u)^α,
  $$ where $\mathrm{dist}$ stands for Euclidean distance and $\mathrm{Aff}(F)$ is the affine hull of $F$. We show that the threshold of the exponent $α\in\mathbb{R}$ for $u$ to have infinite slope at $F$ is $α\leq 2d-n$. For the first two equations, we also show that no solution exists when $α\leq 2d-2n$. Moreover, when $Ω$ satisfies the ``exterior cone condition with a $d$-dimensional ridge'' at $F$, both thresholds are sharp for the first equation, and the infinite-slope threshold is sharp for the last equation.

AI.tldr: The paper studies convex solutions with zero boundary values to three Monge-Ampère equations with power-type right-hand sides involving distances to affine hulls, boundaries, or the solution itself, and determines sharp exponent thresholds for infinite slope at flat boundary pieces and for nonexistence of solutions.
AI.motivation: Understanding boundary behavior and solvability of Monge-Ampère equations near flat boundary pieces is important, particularly how the geometry of a d-dimensional flat boundary component affects singularity and existence thresholds.
AI.method: Analyze convex solutions on bounded convex domains with d-dimensional flat boundary pieces, with right-hand sides given by powers of Euclidean distances to Aff(F), to the boundary, or to -u, and derive exponent thresholds using geometric conditions such as the exterior cone condition with a d-dimensional ridge.
AI.result: The threshold exponent for infinite slope at F is α ≤ 2d − n. For the first two equations, no solution exists when α ≤ 2d − 2n. Under the exterior cone condition with a d-dimensional ridge, both thresholds are sharp for the first equation, and the infinite-slope threshold is sharp for the last equation.
AI.conclusion: The geometry of flat boundary pieces governs sharp exponent thresholds for boundary singularity and existence of convex Monge-Ampère solutions, with the exterior cone condition ensuring optimality of these thresholds.

title: On sharp singular Moser-Trudinger type inequalities and applications to zero mass $(p,Q)$-Laplace subelliptic equations in the Heisenberg group
summary:
This article establishes a sharp singular Moser-Trudinger type inequality in a new function space and explores a concentration-compactness principle in the Heisenberg group, inspired by P.\textcolor{blue}{-}L. Lions. We analyze the equivalence of sharp critical and subcritical singular Moser-Trudinger inequalities, focusing on their asymptotic behavior and connections between their suprema. Additionally, we apply the mountain pass theorem to demonstrate the existence of positive ground state solutions for zero mass $(p, Q)$-Laplace subelliptic equations with singular exponential nonlinearity for the following equation: $$
  -Δ_{H,p} u-Δ_{H,Q} u=\frac{f(ξ,u)}{r(ξ)^\vartheta}\quad\text{in}\quad \mathbb{H}^n, $$ with $1<p<Q$, $\vartheta\in(0,Q)$, $Q=2n+2$, the function $r(\cdot)$ is called the Korányi norm in $\mathbb{H}^n$ and the nonlinearity $f:\mathbb{H}^n\times \mathbb{R}\to \mathbb{R}$ is a Carathéodory function, which behaves like $\exp{(α|s|^{\frac{Q}{Q-1}})}$ as $|s|\to~+\infty$ for some $α>0$.

AI.tldr: The paper proves a sharp singular Moser-Trudinger inequality in a new function space on the Heisenberg group, establishes a concentration-compactness principle, and applies the mountain pass theorem to show existence of positive ground state solutions for zero mass (p, Q)-Laplace subelliptic equations with singular exponential nonlinearity.
AI.motivation: Sharp singular Moser-Trudinger inequalities and concentration-compactness principles are fundamental tools in nonlinear analysis, inspired by P.-L. Lions. Extending these to the Heisenberg group and applying them to subelliptic equations with exponential nonlinearity addresses a gap in understanding critical exponential problems in this non-Euclidean setting.
AI.method: The authors establish a sharp Moser-Trudinger type inequality in a new function space on the Heisenberg group, analyze the equivalence of sharp critical and subcritical singular inequalities via asymptotic behavior and suprema connections, develop a concentration-compactness principle, and apply the mountain pass theorem to prove existence of positive ground state solutions.
AI.result: A sharp singular Moser-Trudinger inequality is obtained, equivalence between critical and subcritical singular inequalities is analyzed, a concentration-compactness principle in the Heisenberg group is derived, and existence of positive ground state solutions for zero mass (p, Q)-Laplace subelliptic equations with singular exponential nonlinearity is demonstrated.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a foundational framework for singular exponential critical problems on the Heisenberg group, extending Moser-Trudinger and concentration-compactness theory and guaranteeing ground state solutions for a class of zero mass subelliptic equations with exponential nonlinearity.

title: A Complete Proof of Mueller--Ho Conjecture
summary:
For $s>0$, and $z\in\mathbb H=\{z=x+iy:y>0\}$, define
  $θ(s;z)=\sum_{m,n\in\mathbb Z}e^{-πs\big(m^2y+\frac{(mx-n)^2}{y}\big)}$ and $
  J(z;a,b)=\sum_{m,n\in\mathbb Z}e^{-π\big(m^2y+\frac{(mx-n)^2}{y}\big)}
  \cos\bigl(2π(ma+nb)\bigr)$ for the classical and shifted theta functions (Gaussian lattice sums), respectively.
  We prove that, up to the modular group, there exist three thresholds $0<α_a<α_b<α_c<1$ such that \begin{equation}\aligned\nonumber \Minima_{z\in\mathbb H,\,(a,b)\in\mathbb R^2}\Big(θ(1;z)+αJ(z;a,b)\Big)= \begin{cases} \;\big(e^{iπ/{3}};1/3,1/3\big), &\hbox{if}\;\; α\in[0,α_a),\\ \;\big(e^{iπ/{3}};1/3,1/3\big)\;\hbox{or}\;\big(e^{i{\varphi_{α_a}}};1/2,1/2\big), &\hbox{if}\;\; α=α_a,\\ \;\big(e^{i{\varphi_α}};1/2,1/2\big),\;\varphi_α\in(\varphi_{α_a},\fracπ{2}),\;\; &\hbox{if}\;\; α\in(α_a,α_b),\\ \;\big(i;1/2,1/2\big),\; &\hbox{if}\;\; α\in[α_b,α_c],\\ \;\big(iy_α;1/2,1/2\big),\; y_α\in(1,\sqrt3],\;\;y_1=\sqrt3,\;\;&\hbox{if}\;\; α\in(α_c,1], \end{cases} \endaligned\end{equation} where the complex variable $z$ and vector $(a,b)$, represent the total vortex shapes and relative positions of the two-component Bose gas, respectively. Consequently, this completely proves the conjecture of Mueller and Ho~\cite{Mue2002} (2002) arising in Bose--Einstein condensates.

AI.tldr: This paper proves the Mueller–Ho conjecture from 2002 on vortex lattice configurations in two-component Bose–Einstein condensates by minimizing classical and shifted theta functions over the modular group, establishing exact thresholds for the optimal lattice shapes.
AI.motivation: The Mueller–Ho conjecture (2002) concerning the vortex shapes and relative positions in rotating two-component Bose gases remained unresolved. This work aims to settle it rigorously via theta function minimization.
AI.method: Define the classical theta function θ(s;z) and the shifted theta function J(z;a,b), then minimize the combined functional θ(1;z)+αJ(z;a,b) over z∈ℍ and (a,b)∈ℝ², up to the modular group, analyzing transitions across thresholds.
AI.result: Three thresholds 0<α_a<α_b<α_c<1 characterize the minimizers: for α∈[0,α_a) the minimizer is (e^{iπ/3};1/3,1/3); at α_a a coexistence occurs with (e^{iφ_{α_a}};1/2,1/2); for α∈(α_a,α_b) it is (e^{iφ_α};1/2,1/2); for α∈[α_b,α_c] it is (i;1/2,1/2); and for α∈(α_c,1] it is (iy_α;1/2,1/2) with y_α∈(1,√3].
AI.conclusion: The full classification of minimizers completely proves the Mueller–Ho conjecture arising in Bose–Einstein condensates.

title: A Schiffer-type inverse obstacle problem for the planar Schrödinger equation with a single measurement
summary: We prove a single measurement uniqueness result for interior sound-soft obstacles in the planar Schrödinger equation with an unknown surrounding potential. For any two configurations with different obstacles, we construct a boundary datum for which the corresponding Neumann measurements differ. The full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map uniquely determines both the obstacle and the potential. The obstacles may have several connected components, and no convexity or analyticity assumptions are imposed. Neither potential is required to be known near the measurement boundary.

AI.tldr: A single boundary measurement uniquely determines both an interior sound-soft obstacle and the surrounding unknown potential in the 2D Schrödinger equation.
AI.motivation: Inverse problems for the Schrödinger equation typically assume one unknown (obstacle or potential). Here both are unknown simultaneously, and no a priori info (convexity, analyticity, known potential near boundary) is available.
AI.method: Constructive boundary-data approach: for any two configurations with distinct obstacles, build a Dirichlet datum whose Neumann measurements differ, yielding uniqueness for the full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map.
AI.result: The full Dirichlet-to-Neumann map uniquely determines both obstacle and potential; identities hold even at the single-measurement level.
AI.conclusion: Obstacles with multiple connected components are handled with no convexity/analyticity assumptions, and the potential need not be known near the measurement boundary.

title: Normalized solutions to 1-Laplace equations with critical growth term
summary: We study normalized solutions to the 1-Laplace equation \[ -\mbox{div}\left(\frac{Du}{|Du|}\right)+λ\frac{u}{|u|}=f(u)+|u|^{1^*-2}u,\quad\mbox{in}~ \mathbb{R}^N \] subject to the constraint $\int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u| \, \mbox{d}x=m$, where $N\geq2$, $1^*=\frac{N}{N-1}$ is the critical Sobolev exponent for the embedding from BV into $L^p$, $λ, m\in\mathbb{R}^+$ and $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$ is a continuous nonlinear perturbation. We first establish a Pohozaev-type identity for the equation and use it to study the associated critical energy, and then prove the existence of normalized solutions via nonsmooth critical point theory. A key feature of our approach is the proof of the existence of a Palais-Smale sequence for a Lipschitz continuous functional under a Lipschitz continuous constraint. This is significantly different in methodology from previous problems with $C^2$ constraint.

AI.tldr: The paper studies normalized solutions to a 1-Laplace equation in R^N with critical Sobolev exponent and an L^1 constraint, proving existence via nonsmooth critical point theory.
AI.motivation: Analyzing normalized solutions to the 1-Laplace equation is challenging because the problem is nonsmooth and involves a critical exponent for the BV-to-L^p embedding, and prior methods relying on C^2 constraints do not apply.
AI.method: The authors establish a Pohozaev-type identity to study the critical energy, then prove existence of normalized solutions using nonsmooth critical point theory, including a Palais-Smale sequence for a Lipschitz continuous functional under a Lipschitz continuous constraint.
AI.result: A Pohozaev-type identity is derived and used to analyze the associated critical energy, and existence of normalized solutions is proven.
AI.conclusion: The work extends normalized solution theory to the nonsmooth 1-Laplace setting, with the Lipschitz-constraint Palais-Smale argument marking a methodological departure from C^2-constraint approaches.

title: Global regularity and infinite Prandtl-number limit for 2D Boussinesq temperature patches in $W^{k,\infty}$ and $C^{k,γ}$: lower-order case
summary: We study global regularity and the infinite Prandtl number limit for temperature patches of the two-dimensional nondiffusive Boussinesq system on $\mathbb R^2$, with velocity dissipation $Λ^{2α}$, $\frac12<α\leq1$. We establish global well-posedness for $θ_0\in L^1\cap L^\infty$ and divergence-free $u_0\in W^{1,p}$, $2\leq p<\infty$. Under suitable profile and striated regularity assumptions, we prove global persistence of $C^{1,γ}$ and $C^{2,γ}$ patch boundaries for every $0<γ\leq1$, allowing nonconstant profiles and including the Lipschitz endpoints $W^{2,\infty}$ and $W^{3,\infty}$. The velocity gradient and boundary regularity estimates are uniform in $\mathrm{Pr}\in[1,\infty)$ on each finite time interval. Uniform global $L^r$ velocity bounds hold for suitable finite $r$ when $α<1$, and at $α=1$ for zero-mean initial temperatures with finite first absolute moment. Such bounds fail at $α=1$ for compactly supported nonzero-mean data. For temperature patches, we justify the infinite Prandtl number limit in the original frame when $α<1$ or the initial temperature has zero mean, and in a moving frame otherwise. The limit is the unique normalized global weak solution of the (fractional) Stokes-transport system and, importantly, preserves the patch structure and boundary regularity.

AI.tldr: Global regularity and infinite Prandtl limit for temperature patches in the 2D nondiffusive Boussinesq system with fractional velocity dissipation on R^2.
AI.motivation: To understand global well-posedness, boundary regularity persistence, and the infinite Prandtl number limit for temperature patches in a nondiffusive Boussinesq system with fractional dissipation.
AI.method: Analysis of the 2D nondiffusive Boussinesq system with velocity dissipation Λ^{2α}, 1/2<α≤1; establishing global well-posedness and uniform-in-Prandtl gradient/boundary estimates under profile and striated regularity assumptions.
AI.result: Global well-posedness for θ0∈L1∩L∞ and divergence-free u0∈W^{1,p}; persistence of C^{1,γ} and C^{2,γ} patch boundaries for all 0<γ≤1 including Lipschitz endpoints; uniform-in-Prandtl estimates; uniform global Lr velocity bounds for α<1, and at α=1 with zero-mean/finite first moment data (failing for compactly supported nonzero-mean data).
AI.conclusion: The infinite Prandtl limit is justified (original frame for α<1 or zero mean, moving frame otherwise), yielding the unique normalized global weak solution of the Stokes-transport system while preserving patch structure and boundary regularity.

title: Best Constants for Anisotropic Moser-Trudinger Inequalities with the Exact Growth Condition and Their Applications
summary: We investigate the best constants associated with several types of Moser--Trudinger inequalities within the framework of the Finsler metric in $\mathbb{R}^n$. By employing a convex-symmetrization-free approach, we first establish both the critical and subcritical anisotropic singular Moser--Trudinger inequalities. We further study anisotropic Moser--Trudinger inequalities in both singular and nonsingular cases under the exact growth condition, highlighting the optimality of the best constant as well as the sharp exponent appearing in the denominator. To further enrich the theory, we introduce quasi-conformal-type transformations adapted to the Finsler metric setting to derive several new variants of such inequalities. We also characterize the attainability and nonattainability of maximizers for a generalized version of anisotropic Moser--Trudinger inequalities with the exact growth and explicitly determine the corresponding supremum values. As an application of these inequalities, we analyze the existence and nonexistence of positive ground state solutions to a class of $n$-Finsler-Laplace equations involving constant potential in $\mathbb{R}^n$, where the nonlinearity exhibits a critical exponential growth at infinity.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes best constants for various anisotropic (Finsler-metric) Moser–Trudinger inequalities, including critical/subcritical singular cases and exact growth conditions, and applies them to n-Finsler-Laplace equations.
AI.motivation: Moser–Trudinger inequalities and their best constants are central in analysis, and extending them to the anisotropic Finsler metric setting—avoiding convex symmetrization—remains an open and important direction.
AI.method: A convex-symmetrization-free approach; establishment of critical and subcritical anisotropic singular Moser–Trudinger inequalities; study under exact growth conditions; introduction of quasi-conformal-type transformations adapted to the Finsler metric.
AI.result: Optimality of best constants and sharp denominator exponents are shown; new inequality variants are derived; attainability/nonattainability of maximizers is characterized with explicit supremum values; existence and nonexistence of positive ground states for n-Finsler-Laplace equations with critical exponential growth are obtained.
AI.conclusion: The paper enriches anisotropic Moser–Trudinger theory with optimal constants and sharp results, providing a foundation for studying critical exponential-growth problems in Finsler settings.

title: Endpoint Compactness and Finite-Energy Weak Solutions for the 2D Isothermal Compressible Navier-Stokes
summary: We prove global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the 2D isothermal compressible Navier--Stokes equations in bounded $C^2$ domains with no-slip boundary conditions. The initial data are arbitrary in the natural energy class, allowing vacuum and unbounded density. This resolves the isothermal endpoint $γ=1$ of the classical 2D finite-energy renormalized existence theory for power-law pressures. We develop a new endpoint compactness argument based on a truncation-independent integrable bound for centered density oscillations. This argument yields strong $L^1$ compactness of the approximating densities at the natural energy level.

AI.tldr: Global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions for 2D isothermal compressible Navier-Stokes equations (γ=1) in bounded C² domains with no-slip boundaries, for arbitrary initial data in the natural energy class allowing vacuum and unbounded density.
AI.motivation: The isothermal endpoint γ=1 of the classical 2D finite-energy renormalized existence theory for power-law pressures was previously unresolved; existing methods failed at this critical exponent.
AI.method: A new endpoint compactness argument based on a truncation-independent integrable bound for centered density oscillations, yielding strong L¹ compactness of approximating densities at the natural energy level.
AI.result: Established global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions for arbitrary initial data in the natural energy class, allowing vacuum and unbounded density.
AI.conclusion: The isothermal endpoint γ=1 of the 2D finite-energy renormalized existence theory is resolved, completing the power-law pressure picture.

title: Estimates on Fully Nonlinear Elliptic Equations with Unrectifiable Exceptional Gradient Sets
summary: We study fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations that are imposed only when the gradients of solutions lie outside a closed ball and a closed purely one-unrectifiable set that can be unbounded. We prove Harnack inequalities and Hölder regularity estimates for viscosity solutions, with constants independent of the exceptional set. The proofs use the geometry of the contact sets in the cusp and barrier arguments to exclude exceptional gradients. We also provide examples and counterexamples showing the role of pure one-unrectifiability. Materials and proofs are presented in detail to ensure the paper is fully self-contained and accessible to a broad audience.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes Harnack inequalities and Hölder regularity for viscosity solutions of fully nonlinear uniformly elliptic equations imposed only outside a closed ball and a closed purely one-unrectifiable set, with constants independent of the exceptional set.
AI.motivation: Regularity theory typically assumes equations hold everywhere. This work addresses equations that are only enforced when gradients avoid an exceptional set, extending classical results to settings with non-smooth, possibly unbounded exceptional gradient sets.
AI.method: Proofs exploit the geometry of contact sets in the cusp and employ barrier arguments to exclude exceptional gradients, handling the closed ball and purely one-unrectifiable set as the exceptional regions.
AI.result: The authors prove Harnack inequalities and Hölder regularity estimates for viscosity solutions, with constants independent of the exceptional set. They also give examples and counterexamples demonstrating the role of pure one-unrectifiability.
AI.conclusion: Pure one-unrectifiability of the exceptional set is essential to the regularity results. The paper is made fully self-contained and accessible to a broad audience.

title: On the Gage-Hamilton-Grayson Theorem for free boundary curves
summary: We provide an alternative and independent proof of the analogue of the Gage-Hamilton-Grayson Theorem for embedded free boundary curve shortening flows in a convex planar domain established by Langford-Zhu. Our proof is based on blowup arguments introduced by B. White in his work on mean-convex mean curvature flow.

AI.tldr: An alternative, independent proof of the Gage-Hamilton-Grayson theorem analogue for embedded free boundary curve shortening flows in a convex planar domain.
AI.motivation: The result was previously established by Langford-Zhu; an independent proof would provide new insight and verification of the theorem.
AI.method: Uses blowup arguments introduced by B. White in his work on mean-convex mean curvature flow.
AI.result: Re-derives the Langford-Zhu theorem via the alternative blowup approach.
AI.conclusion: The blowup technique offers a valid, independent route to the free boundary curve shortening flow result.

title: On Cylindrical singularities of minimal hypersurfaces
summary: In a neighborhood of the origin in $\mathbb{R}^9$, we construct a minimal hypersurface with respect to a smooth conformally Euclidean metric, whose singular set consists of the origin and a sequence of isolated singular points converging to it. At each of the isolated singular points the hypersurface has the unique tangent cone $C_{4,3}$, the cone over $S^4(\sqrt{4/7})\times S^3(\sqrt{3/7})$, whereas at the origin its unique tangent cone is the cone $C_{3,3}\times\mathbb{R}$. The metric is Euclidean near each isolated singular point and agrees with the Euclidean metric to infinite order at the origin. A key step, of independent interest, is the construction of an entire stationary hypersurface in Euclidean $\mathbb{R}^9$ with exactly one singular point at the origin, at which its unique tangent cone is $C_{4,3}$, and whose unique tangent cone at infinity is $C_{3,3}\times\mathbb{R}$.

AI.tldr: Construction of a minimal hypersurface in R^9 (conformally Euclidean metric) whose singular set is the origin plus a sequence of isolated singular points converging to it, with prescribed tangent cones.
AI.motivation: Study the structure of singular sets of minimal hypersurfaces and the possible tangent cones, extending known examples of singular sets to include accumulation points.
AI.method: Construct a minimal hypersurface near the origin in R^9 with respect to a smooth conformally Euclidean metric; use a key auxiliary construction of an entire stationary hypersurface in Euclidean R^9 with exactly one singular point.
AI.result: The hypersurface has singular set {origin} ∪ a sequence of isolated singular points converging to the origin. At each isolated point the unique tangent cone is C_{4,3} = cone over S^4(√(4/7))×S^3(√(3/7)); at the origin the tangent cone is C_{3,3}×R. The metric is Euclidean near each isolated singular point and agrees with Euclidean metric to infinite order at the origin.
AI.conclusion: Provides a new example of a minimal hypersurface with non-isolated (accumulating) singularities and prescribed tangent cones, highlighting the role of the entire stationary hypersurface with unique tangent cones at the origin and at infinity.

title: Existence and Uniqueness of Viscosity Solutions for Stochastic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman Equations
summary:
We study stochastic Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equations arising from stochastic optimal control problems with random coefficients and possible degenerateness. The viscosity solution is reformulated by using adapted smooth random test fields that touch on stopped space--time neighborhoods almost surely.
  The state coefficients are predictable, with no continuity assumption on their dependence on the underlying Brownian path. Under linear growth of locally Lipschitz drift and diffusion coefficients, polynomial growth of the running and terminal cost coefficients, and a nonempty separable metric space-valued control set, we show that the value function is the unique viscosity solution in this formulation among adapted continuous fields with square-integrable random polynomial growth bounds. The comparison proof constructs adapted fields from controlled trajectories and spatially shaken conditional values, using a weak semimartingale decomposition and regularization of its positive finite-variation part. In particular, the uniqueness allows for diffusion coefficients being random, degenerate, and depending on time, state, and control, whereas earlier uniqueness results of Qiu [SIAM J. Control Optim. 56 (2018), pp. 3708--3730] and Qiu and Zhang [Ann. Appl. Probab. 33 (2023), pp. 889--930] were obtained under additional structural restrictions on the diffusion coefficient, such as determinism combined with either superparabolicity or independence of the state and controls.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes uniqueness of viscosity solutions for stochastic HJB equations from optimal control with random, possibly degenerate coefficients, using adapted smooth random test fields.
AI.motivation: Prior uniqueness results (Qiu 2018; Qiu-Zhang 2023) required extra structural restrictions on the diffusion coefficient. This work removes such restrictions to handle general random, degenerate, and control/state-dependent diffusions.
AI.method: Uses a viscosity solution framework with adapted smooth random test fields touching on stopped space-time neighborhoods almost surely. The comparison proof builds adapted fields from controlled trajectories and shaken conditional values, via weak semimartingale decomposition and regularization of its positive finite-variation part.
AI.result: Under linear growth of locally Lipschitz drift/diffusion, polynomial growth of running/terminal costs, and a separable metric control set, the value function is the unique viscosity solution among adapted continuous fields with square-integrable random polynomial growth bounds.
AI.conclusion: Uniqueness holds even when the diffusion coefficient is random, degenerate, and depends on time, state, and control, extending earlier work beyond determinism or independence/superparabolicity assumptions.

title: Backstepping Stabilization of a Hyperbolic System with a Zero Characteristic Speed
summary: This paper investigates the boundary stabilization of a linear hyperbolic system with a zero characteristic speed. We address a case that cannot be stabilized by proportional boundary feedback and develop a backstepping design for the critical setting where the zero-speed subsystem has no intrinsic dissipation. To this end, we construct a Volterra transformation leading to a nonstandard integro-differential target system. Its asymptotic stability in L2 is established by both the Lyapunov-LaSalle method and a spectral semigroup argument. The backstepping kernel equations are explicitly solved, yielding an explicit boundary feedback law that asymptotically stabilizes the original system. Numerical simulations are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed control design.

AI.tldr: The paper designs a backstepping boundary controller for a linear hyperbolic system containing a zero-speed subsystem without intrinsic dissipation — a critical case not stabilizable by proportional boundary feedback — and proves L2 asymptotic stability.
AI.motivation: Some linear hyperbolic systems with a zero characteristic speed cannot be stabilized by proportional boundary feedback, especially when the zero-speed subsystem lacks intrinsic dissipation. This critical setting calls for a more sophisticated design method.
AI.method: A backstepping design is developed. A Volterra transformation is constructed that maps the system to a nonstandard integro-differential target system. Stability is proven via both the Lyapunov-LaSalle method and a spectral semigroup argument. The backstepping kernel equations are solved explicitly, giving an explicit boundary feedback law.
AI.result: L2 asymptotic stability of the target system is established, and the explicit kernel solution yields an explicit boundary feedback law that asymptotically stabilizes the original system. Numerical simulations confirm the effectiveness of the control design.
AI.conclusion: Backstepping can stabilize a zero-speed hyperbolic subsystem without intrinsic dissipation, where proportional boundary feedback fails, using a nonstandard Volterra transformation and explicit kernel solution.

title: Barron Optimal Transport I: Generative Modeling
summary:
Motivated by recent applications in generative modeling and sampling, we introduce a framework for optimal measure transport where cost captures the notion of neural network complexity. In transport-based generative models, samples from a reference distribution (e.g. Gaussian) are mapped to samples of a target distribution along ordinary or stochastic differential equations. These are implemented as deep residual networks when discretized in time, where each hidden layer approximates the associated instantaneous velocity. Thus, given a pair of target and reference measures, a natural question is to search for the most efficient neural representation that implements this transport.
  Our starting point is the kinetic formulation of OT, due to Benamou and Brenier. We replace the average kinetic $L^2$ energy by the \emph{Barron} energy \cite{bach2017breaking, ma2022barron}, a natural norm which measures the complexity of representing a given vector field with a neural hidden layer, and which captures the adaptive properties of feature learning. This defines a metric on the space of probability measures, complementing existing Wasserstein and Stein geometries.
  In this work we examine the properties of this metric in the context of generative modeling. As a first application, we quantify the suboptimality of diffusion generative modeling in the Barron geometry by establishing super-polynomial score approximation lower bounds for data generated by neural network pushforwards of the Gaussian. We then investigate the benefit of adaptivity as a way to study alternative generative models. In a companion paper \cite{companionpaper} we leverage the Barron transport geometry for sampling applications, extending the scope of Stein variational gradient methods via feature adaptation.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a Barron-energy optimal transport framework that measures neural network complexity of measure transport, and uses it to prove super-polynomial lower bounds on score approximation for diffusion generative models.
AI.motivation: Transport-based generative models (diffusion, residual networks) map a reference distribution to a target via ODEs/SDEs, but there is no principled way to find the most efficient neural representation of that transport. Existing Wasserstein and Stein geometries do not capture the adaptive, feature-learning cost of neural networks, so the authors seek a geometry that reflects neural complexity.
AI.method: They start from the Benamou-Brenier kinetic formulation of optimal transport and replace the average kinetic L^2 energy with the Barron energy, a norm measuring the complexity of representing a vector field by a neural hidden layer with adaptive feature learning. This yields a new metric (the Barron transport geometry) on the space of probability measures.
AI.result: They establish properties of this metric for generative modeling. In particular, they quantify the suboptimality of diffusion generative modeling in the Barron geometry by proving super-polynomial score approximation lower bounds for data given by neural network pushforwards of the Gaussian. They also analyze the benefit of adaptivity for alternative generative models.
AI.conclusion: The Barron transport geometry complements existing Wasserstein and Stein geometries and exposes limitations of diffusion models, while adaptivity offers a route to better generative models. A companion paper extends this geometry to sampling via feature-adaptive Stein variational gradient methods.
